sections.h2: Your options for selling in Schertz
sections.html:
Schertz sellers tend to choose among an agent, a sale handled on your own and a cash offer that takes the house exactly as it is. The state of the roof and systems, your deadline and your tolerance for a lower price do most of the deciding.

Schertz straddles the Bexar and Guadalupe line, and the city has since reached into Comal County. That means a single street can answer to more than one county office, so learn which county holds your parcel before any signature.

Gather written offers and set each beside an agent's estimate of your net after commission and fix up costs. That gap is the real price of closing fast.

Schertz began as a rail stop on Farm Road 78, two miles southeast of Interstate 35 and nineteen miles west of Seguin. It incorporated in 1958 with 351 residents. The count was 18,694 in 2000 and 36,244 by 2015. A city that doubled in fifteen years has many newer subdivisions, and buyers often weigh a Schertz house against similar ones in neighboring suburbs. When you talk to buyers, name your subdivision and be straight about the roof, the mechanical systems and the lot.

sections.h2: Which county and school district serve you
sections.html:
Your tax statement answers that. Guadalupe County parcels go through the Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose member list includes the City of Schertz and Schertz-Cibolo-UC ISD. Parcels in Bexar or Comal County use those counties' districts.

The bill lists the taxing units, and a buyer's agent will want that list, so read it first.

  • Value, exemptions and protests: the appraisal district.
  • Bills and payments: the county tax office.
  • The city has its own rate, and the school district gets a line of its own.

For the rate on your own parcel, call the county tax office or the city. A neighbor's bill may not match.

The City of Schertz Inspections Division issues building permits and registers contractors for construction inside the city, and it reviews plans for work in the extraterritorial jurisdiction where that applies. Call (210) 619-1750 or write inspections@schertz.com. The division also investigates alleged building code complaints and supports the Unified Development Code.

Outdoor building work runs weekdays from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The city prohibits outdoor work on Sundays. The division's counter hours follow the same schedule.

Permits matter at sale time. If a room, deck or wall opening went in without one, a buyer's inspector may spot it. An as is cash buyer will likely price that risk, while the lender behind a conventional buyer may ask for a fix first. Ask the division what is on file before you list.

sections.h2: Working with the Guadalupe Appraisal District
sections.html:
You will find a parcel search portal on the district's site, along with online filing for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions. Paper forms are still offered at the offices. Its Appraisal Review Board hears appeals at the main office in Seguin, and a taxpayer liaison officer attends on hearing days. Reach the liaison at 830.303.3313 extension 309.

One mail warning applies. Since late December 2025, USPS postmarks in Texas show the date of automated processing instead of the day you drop an item off. A paper form with a deadline should go to a post office counter, where you can request a hand-stamped postmark.

Not sure who to call? The district answers value, exemption and protest questions, while the tax office takes bills and payments.

Every January 1 fixes the property's value and starts that year's tax lien.

Bills arrive near October 1, with January 31 as the deadline. Any balance left at closing is paid from your proceeds, so request the county's payoff number early.

sections.h2: Behind on the mortgage or the taxes
sections.html:
Before a Texas lender can foreclose, a notice of sale has to go out, and the auction happens on a first Tuesday. A private sale ahead of that day can protect equity that an auction might send to junior lien holders first.

Overdue taxes add cost quickly. Penalties begin February 1 and reach 12 percent by July 1. A few collectors offer installment plans on a residence homestead, so phone the tax office sooner rather than later.

Offers rarely look alike on paper. One buyer pays title and recording costs, another expects you to. One closes in days, another needs weeks for financing. List each in a simple chart: price, repair credits, who covers closing costs, closing date and what happens if the title search turns up a lien. Add the county tax balance you will owe at closing, since it comes out of your proceeds no matter who buys. The highest number is not always the largest check.

sections.h2: Splitting the tax bill at closing
sections.html: Most Schertz sales settle the year's tax by days of ownership, though your contract has the final say. Suppose you close in the spring: the new bill will not exist until October 1, so the title company works from the prior figure and adjusts later if the parties agreed to. Read that clause before you sign. If you sell after the bill arrives and have not paid it, expect the whole amount to be withheld from your check until the county confirms the payoff. Keep a copy of the receipt when you do pay, and give your buyer the account number so they can find the parcel on the district portal.

sections.h2: A note on parcels near the county line
sections.html: If your lot is close to the line, call the Guadalupe Appraisal District or the other county's district and ask them to confirm the account number, then check that the legal description on your deed matches. A mismatch between the deed and the tax record is a common cause of closing delays. Neighbors who share a fence can still have different districts, and the title company will want the one that applies to you. Keep the confirmation email or a note of who you spoke to.

A rented house can be sold. Some buyers will keep the lease running, and otherwise you can end the tenancy first. Ending it means written notice, a justice court case and, after final judgment, a writ of possession.

If the tenant pays on time and keeps the place clean, rent can continue right up to closing. If rent has stopped, ask whether the buyer will deal with the removal after closing.

A deed reaches the public record through the county clerk, after a notary or other authorized officer witnesses the signature. Since Schertz crosses county lines, double check the clerk before you go.

An inherited house follows whatever route the estate allows.

  • If a will went through probate, an executor's deed or court order follows.
  • When real estate liens are the estate's only debts, a muniment of title can transfer the house.
  • An heirship affidavit is only a sworn statement filed with the clerk, and buyers or title companies may refuse to rely on it.

Before listing, ask a title company which route applies.

Cash deals follow a short path. You accept in writing, and the title company opens a file, searches the parcel for liens and open tax, and, because Schertz touches three counties, confirms which clerk will record the deed. Next comes a closing date, a signing in front of a notary and your proceeds, minus any tax balance. Take photo ID and the deed or estate papers with you, and request the settlement statement a day before. With no lender on the buyer's side, nothing waits on an appraisal or loan approval, and that is where the time is saved.

faqs.a: Three, in practice: Bexar, Comal and Guadalupe. The city sits on the Bexar and Guadalupe line and spread into Comal County.

faqs.q: What if work on my Schertz house lacked a permit?
faqs.a: You can still sell, but expect questions. The Inspections Division issues permits and can be reached at (210) 619-1750.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax at a Schertz closing?
faqs.a: The contract sets the split, often by days of ownership. Get the amount owed from the county tax office before closing day.

faqs.q: What happens after the January 31 tax deadline?
faqs.a: The bill is delinquent from February 1, and penalty and interest begin. The penalty grows each month until it hits 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Must a Schertz house be repaired before a cash sale?
faqs.a: Often not. Cash buyers frequently take houses in present condition, so weigh that offer against an agent's projection after repairs and commission.
